..
Next 7 Days...

The dog days of summer continue as our weather for the next week
will remain dominated by a strong ridge ever so slowly migrating
eastwards. Today will be another hot day for the entire region
with most locations seeing their highest temps of the stretch 
this afternoon. 700mb temperatures across the region are forecast 
to be in the upper teens but there is some discrepancy amongst 
models with the latest runs. The ECMWF notably has 700mb temps 
consistently 2C lower than the GFS does which would mean that some
places my struggle to see 100F this afternoon. Given the strength
of the ridge in place, the current trend in temperatures so far
today, and the highs we hit yesterday the warmer temps seem like 
the more believable outcome. That being said, there was a decent 
amount of mid to high level clouds, along with some smoke, around 
the region this morning that is slowly clearing out which could 
help negate some solar daytime heating. Places in the eastern CWA 
should be able to hit tipple digits easy today however, locations 
in the western 2/3 of the forecast area seem like the final piece 
of the puzzle may just be the afternoon convection and what time 
that gets going. Regardless, it will still be quite hot for 
everyone today.

Even with our dew points in the 50s F for much of the area today,
temps climbing to near or above 100F will bring RH values down
into the teens or lower this afternoon. Also, the warm night last
night only allowed for modest recoveries at best. With record 
highs in jeopardy and the RH values quite low, fire weather 
concerns continue today. These concerns will be further amplified
by the potential for convection this afternoon and evening. Model
soundings across the CWA show textbook inveerted-v soundings with
many locations completely dry adiabatic up through the 500mb 
level. With a decent shortwave in conjunction with the terrain 
kicking off storms later today and the sufficient moisture, 
convection should not have any issue getting going. The two main 
concerns with these storms will be winds and the potential for dry
lightning. Even if the mid levels are very well saturated, rain 
with the weaker cells may struggle to fall through 3-4km of dry 
air. This setup is also textbook for dry microbursts and strong, 
far reaching outflow boundaries. All of which are cause for 
concern when it comes to fire starts and spread. Be extra cautious
to not spark a fire today and report any sparks that you do see.

In terms of severe storms today, the the threats for today are
pretty much only what I mentioned above. Long straight hodographs
may support upscale growth into a few lines of convection by the
evening hours as the storms make their way through and east of  
Billings. ML CAPE today may reach 1000 J/Kg at best in the western
part of the CWA but most of that will be concentrated in the mid 
levels in the form of long/skinny CAPE. While this could support 
some hail growth in the stronger storms, the lack of sheer 
combined with the very dry low levels will likely prevent any 
severe hail reaching the ground today. 

Sunday looks to be similar to today in many aspects. While models
and ensembles bring temps down just a skosh, many locations still
have a good chance of touching triple digits, esepcailly in the 
plains of Eastern Montana. We are also looking at another 
potential vort max riding the ridge and aiding in initiating 
convection off of terrin in the afternoon. With another 
inverted-v type sounding, I would not be surprised to see a 
couple of storms kick out severe wind gusts again tomorrow. The 
continued heat, low RH values, and convection will lead to another
day of fire weather concerns. 

The unfortunate news is that there is really no progressive flow 
aloft through the entire work week and thus the ridge shows little
to no signs of changing for several days. Highs in the 90s to 
100s appear likely to stick around into for the remainder of July.
This could pull some monsoonal moisture up into the region with 
the chance for some showers and storms each day, particularly 
near the mountains however coverage will probably be low any 
given day with a low chance for wetting rain.

There is some hope at a potential ridge crasher event next 
weekend which would usher in cooler temps behind it. This could 
bring the potential for gusty winds and maybe some storms as well
so we will need to keep ann eye on this, but for now all 
attention remains on the heat. WMR
